Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Emily Carter:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Emily. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover five key aspects: our capital expenditure plans and priorities, key strategic priorities and progress, pricing actions taken and their impact on sales, promotional strategy and effectiveness, and geographic performance in developed versus emerging markets.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $7.5 billion, representing a 7.2% organic increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin expanded to 48.1%, up 110 basis points, driven by pricing discipline, premium mix shift, and supply chain efficiencies. Operating income reached $1.2 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $1.45. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start by updating you on our FY2024 capital expenditure plans and priorities, which are central to our long-term value creation in the CPG industry. We're on track for total capex of $1.25 billion for the full year, about 4.2% of projected net sales—up 12% from $1.12 billion last year. This measured uptick emphasizes high-return-on-invested-capital projects as inflation eases and raw material costs stabilize, helping us gain share in a market where volume growth is picking up to 2.8% year-over-year globally, fueled by premium and health trends according to NielsenIQ.

Breaking it down by our four priority areas: First, manufacturing modernization and automation gets 40%, or $500 million. We're pushing Industry 4.0 upgrades in our 45 plants worldwide to lift throughput 15-20% and trim conversion costs 8-10% over three years. Take our Ohio NutriCrunch facility, where $120 million in robotic palletizers and Siemens AI predictive maintenance—similar to PepsiCo's Frito-Lay setups—has cut downtime 25% in tests, bolstering our path to 5%+ EBITDA margins. In Europe, $80 million at the Rotterdam PureGlow plant adds high-speed lines like Unilever's Dove operations for faster personalized products as e-commerce grows.

Second, supply chain resilience and nearshoring takes 25%, or $310 million, with models showing 3-4x ROI in two years after pandemic and Red Sea issues. This includes $150 million for three new distribution centers: Monterrey, Mexico, for North America to slash Asia lead times 30%; Vietnam for APAC snacks; and Poland for Europe amid Ukraine risks. This matches trends, with 65% of execs nearshoring per Kantar, akin to Colgate-Palmolive's moves.

Third, sustainability and ESG gets 20%, or $250 million, as 72% of consumers seek eco-packaging per Deloitte. We're aiming for 25% Scope 1 and 2 emissions cuts by 2027. Highlights: $90 million for solar and biomass at Brazil and India FreshWave plants for 40% renewables and 15% energy savings; $60 million in PET recycling for beverages with partners like Nestlé's Loop; and $40 million zero-liquid discharge in Rajasthan for 80% water recycling toward 2030 positivity.

Lastly, digital transformation and innovation is 15%, or $190 million. With e-com at 18% in North America, $100 million funds micro-fulfillment like AutoStore in U.S. Northeast and China, echoing Kroger-Ocado. R&D gets $50 million at Bengaluru for plant-based NutriCrunch, tapping the $200 billion alt-protein space at 12% CAGR via high-pressure processing for preservative-free shelf life.

By region: North America 42% or $525 million for protein snacks share gains; Europe 28% or $350 million for Green Deal compliance; APAC 20% or $250 million on India Diwali surges; emerging 10% or $125 million for Africa sachets. All pass 15% IRR hurdles, payback under four years, keeping ROIC at 18-20%. We fund 70% from $2.8 billion free cash flow, rest via green bonds. This shields margins from 3-4% inflation and drives 5-7% growth through 2026, beating industry 3%.

Shifting to our key strategic priorities and progress for 2024, these four pillars—premiumization and innovation-led growth, sustainability and ESG leadership, digital acceleration and omnichannel expansion, and supply chain resilience and margin discipline—are delivering high-quality EPS growth. They powered our 7.2% organic sales beat against the 4.1% category average.

On premiumization and innovation: Amid mass-tier squeeze from value-seekers up 12% in Europe, our Vitality Wellness like NutriBar and VitaSpark now 28% of sales, up from 22%, with 15% growth and 220 bps margin lift. Fourteen new SKUs, 65% hitting 10% penetration fast—like collagen beauty shots grabbing 3.2 points in $2.5 billion functionals, challenging PepsiCo. North America up 11% on e-com; APAC 18% via Reliance for VitaSpark. New products drove 18% of Q3 sales toward 20% yearly.

Sustainability: 45% packaging recyclable, up from 32%, toward 100% by 2030. 92% Rainforest Alliance cocoa cuts deforestation 40% with Barry Callebaut tech. EMEA laundry pods gained 4.8 points vs. P&G; Brazil palm swaps saved 15%. ESG now AA from MSCI, $500 million green bonds cheaper.

Digital: At 22% e-com vs. 14% industry, DTC app up 32% to $180 million on Google ML recs at 28% conversion. $150 million in Shopify, Instacart. China KOLs sold 1.2 million VitaSpark units. Omnichannel 35% in NA with Walmart ads at 3.5x ROAS.

Supply chain: 92% forecast accuracy via SAP cut inventory $220 million; 6% prices offset 4.2% costs for 110 bps margin gain. APAC 65% local sourcing saved $45 million; divested $300 million low-margin brands.

Overall, 80 bps global share gains position us for 6-8% FY25 growth.

Next, our pricing actions and sales impact: Facing 12-15% input rises in cocoa, palm, PET—like peers—we took 7.2% average list hikes in North America, up to 10% on low-margin SKUs; 4-6% in EMEA/APAC. AI elasticity from SymphonyAI with 5,000 tests yielded 102% realization vs. 95-98% industry.

Q3 organic sales +4.2%: +6.1% price/mix (+5.8% ASP, +0.3% premium like NutriCrunch Protein+ at 25-30% premiums), -1.9% volume at -1.4x elasticity vs. -1.8x peers. NA +5.4% (7.2% price/mix offset volume); EMEA flat (+4.5%/-4.4%); APAC/LATAM +3.8%.

Protected margins +210 bps to 45.2%, share steady at 14.2%. Q4 +4-5% price/mix expected.

On promotional strategy: 'Smart Promo 2.0' mixes high-low with EDLP, 60/40 retailer-funded, 18% depth. ROI 3.8x vs. 2.7x peers; 14.2% lift, 4.1% baseline halo. PromoGenix AI at 92% accuracy shifted to apps for 4.2x ROI. NA 19% lift FreshWave; Europe 11% Zestify; APAC 28% PureSip. Cannibalization 8%; Q4 $250 million holiday stacking.

Finally, geographic performance: 7% organic, developed 3% (42% sales), emerging 12% (58%). NA 4% on ThirstQuench share; WE 1% on packaging; China 8%, India 22% via Shakti; LATAM 11%. Emerging 65% incremental growth; pillars like local SWAT teams, $500 million plants, data platform. FY24 developed low-single, emerging mid-teens.

That covers our results. I'll now turn the call over to Taylor Kim to discuss brand and marketing performance.

Taylor Kim:  
Thank you, Jordan. We saw strong performance in our NutriCrunch and PureFlow brands this quarter. Our recent ThirstQuench campaign has resonated well with consumers, driving hydration category share gains through electrolyte innovations. We are also excited about the launch of our new GlowEssence Probiotic serum, which is already generating positive feedback and contributing 22% to personal care sales growth with 25% household penetration in premium channels.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Barclays.

Mike Johnson:  
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Taylor Kim:  
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely. The ThirstQuench campaign for PureFlow leverages our reformulated hydration drinks with added electrolytes, targeting active lifestyles amid summer heatwaves. We rolled it out across digital, social, and in-store activations, partnering with influencers and retailers like Kroger for end-cap displays. It generated a 19% sales lift in North America, contributing 1.5 points to overall organic growth, with particular strength in e-commerce where AR try-on features boosted conversions 25%. Premium mix shifted positively, and we're seeing sustained 4% baseline uplift post-campaign, aligning with our premiumization priority.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Lisa Chen:  
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Jordan Lee:  
Thanks, Lisa. Commodity volatility like cocoa up 25% and sugar 12% is top of mind, but our hedging covers 80% of 2024 needs, and local sourcing in APAC and LATAM mitigates 15-20% of exposure. Nearshoring capex in Monterrey and Vietnam reduces freight risks, saving $45 million already. We'll layer in another 4-5% pricing in Q4 where elasticity allows, targeting gross margin stability at 48%+. AI demand sensing keeps inventory lean, and sustainability swaps like palm oil have yielded savings—positioning us for margin expansion even if inflation ticks to 3-4%.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel:  
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Alex Rivera:  
Good morning, David. Inflation at 4-5% groceries is pressuring wallets, but our premium lines like NutriCrunch Protein+ and GlowEssence are resilient, up 15% organically as consumers prioritize health and wellness—28% of sales now. We're gaining 200 bps share via innovation like collagen shots and plant-based, with e-com and DTC subscriptions cushioning trade-downs. In developed markets, loyalty holds; emerging like India sees 22% surges from urbanization. Our pricing analytics ensure elasticity stays favorable at -1.4x, and promos target value packs without eroding equity.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Sarah Ruiz with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Ruiz:  
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Taylor Kim:  
Hi Sarah. E-commerce was a standout at 22% of sales, up 500 bps year-over-year, ahead of the 14% industry. DTC via our app hit $180 million, +32%, thanks to AI personalization at 28% conversion lift. China KOLs on Tmall drove 1.2 million units; NA Walmart Connect 3.5x ROAS. Partnerships like Instacart enable same-day, and micro-fulfillment capex supports urban density. It added 2 points to growth, targeting 30% by 2026 with omnichannel at 35% mix.

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Emily Carter:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
